clue.text: He is placed second in this

definitions.meaning: reads as a man, but is the chemical symbol for helium
helium is element number two, so it sits second in the chart that lists every element

explanation.surface: Someone has come second in some competition or ranking.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital on He hides the helium symbol; helium has atomic number 2, the second entry in the chemists' chart.
explanation.definitionFit: The chemists' chart orders substances by atomic number, and helium, with number two, is placed second.

clue.text: Kind of system operating in body, giving directions on timeless principle

definitions.text: Kind of system operating in body

parts.note: E and N are compass points, east and north

indicators.note: less signals dropping, and time is the letter T, so T leaves the word for principle

parts.note: a doctrine is a principle or tenet held as true

explanation.surface: Someone describes a bodily system while laying down a principle.
explanation.walkthrough: T is the standard abbreviation for time.
explanation.definitionFit: The endocrine system is the network of hormone-producing glands working within the body.

clue.text: Clubs in which performers of awful acts may be clapped

definitions.meaning: first meaning: golf clubs with metal heads

definitions.text: in which performers of awful acts may be clapped
definitions.meaning: second meaning: chains or fetters, as in a prisoner clapped in them

explanation.walkthrough: Clapped looks like applause for performers, but it means shackled, as in the phrase clapped in irons.
explanation.definitionFit: Golfers carry metal-headed clubs by this name, and criminals were once shackled in fetters called the same.

clue.text: Clothed English or American guys

parts.note: duds is slang for clothes, and here those clothes are wrapped around the English letter, so this one word both gives the outer piece and shows the containment

explanation.surface: A question of whether some well-dressed men are English or American.
explanation.walkthrough: Duds is informal for clothes; the envelope is implied by the clothes enclosing E.
explanation.definitionFit: Dude is a casual American slang term for a man or fellow.

clue.text: Shortened dress leading to attempt to create instinctive amorous interaction

indicators.note: a shortened word loses its end, so the final letter of the dress is cut off

parts.note: a chemise is a loose, simple dress or shift
to try is to attempt

explanation.surface: A shortened dress is worn in an effort to spark romance.
explanation.walkthrough: Leading to just puts the dress before the attempt.
explanation.definitionFit: Chemistry between two people is their natural mutual attraction or rapport.

clue.text: Product of mine, light and strong — the second one's superfluous for Americans

definitions.text: Product of mine, light and strong
definitions.meaning: a lightweight but strong metal extracted from ore

definitions.text: the second one's superfluous for Americans
definitions.meaning: the second letter I is dropped in the American spelling

explanation.walkthrough: It looks like wordplay removing an I, but it is a description: Americans spell the metal without the second I.
explanation.definitionFit: The metal is mined as bauxite ore, light in weight yet strong, and American usage spells it with one fewer letter.

clue.text: Something that protects quick ascending climber

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: the quick is the sensitive flesh under a fingernail, which a nail covers

explanation.surface: A climber wants protection on a fast ascent.
explanation.walkthrough: Quick here is the noun: the tender flesh under the nail, not speed.
explanation.definitionFit: A liana is a woody vine that climbs trees in tropical forests.

clue.text: Opposite of belligerence characteristic of copper?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: passive acceptance without fighting back
second meaning, whimsical: copper offers very little electrical resistance

explanation.walkthrough: Copper suggests a policeman, but it is the metal; the question mark admits copper does have some resistance, just very little.
explanation.definitionFit: Pacifist submission is passive refusal to fight, and a good electrical conductor barely impedes current.

clue.text: Making unique version of spiral neon sign, omitting one name

indicators.note: a new version of something remakes it, so the remaining letters are rearranged
omitting means leaving out, so the letter for one name is dropped from the phrase

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written
N is the abbreviation for name, and one says just a single N goes

explanation.surface: A shop is making a custom version of a spiral neon sign, leaving out a name.
explanation.walkthrough: Spiral looks like the anagram signal, but it is part of the letters; version of does that job.
explanation.definitionFit: To personalise something is to adapt it so that it is individual to one owner.

clue.text: Dark colour of 11, apart from the tips

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a dull brownish-yellow shade
second meaning: the answer to 11 without its first and last letters is DUCAT, a coin struck from the precious yellow metal in former times

explanation.walkthrough: Strip the ends from the answer at 11 to get DUCAT, a coin made of old gold, which is the second sense.
explanation.definitionFit: The shade is a dark dull yellow, and a ducat was a historic coin struck from precious metal long ago.

clue.text: Eton's head expected to cover up whip in school

indicators.note: the head of a word is its opening letter, so only the start of the school's name is used

parts.note: Eton is the famous English boarding school

indicators.note: the expected word covers the whip, holding it inside

parts.note: something due is expected
a cat, short for cat-o'-nine-tails, is a whip

explanation.surface: Eton's headmaster is expected to hide the cane used in the school.
explanation.definitionFit: To school someone is to teach or train them.

clue.text: One form of carbon, slangily, is unstable

definitions.meaning: first meaning: slang for diamonds, a form of carbon

explanation.walkthrough: Diamond is pure carbon, and rocks is slang for diamonds.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang calls diamonds by this name, and something that sways back and forth is wobbling unsteadily.

clue.text: Reminders of duels, including my boastful claim and swords

indicators.note: the reminders include, or hold inside, the boastful claim

parts.note: scars are the marks left by sword fights
I'm it is a boastful claim to be the best

explanation.surface: A duellist's scars and bragging, along with the swords used.
explanation.definitionFit: Scimitars are curved, single-edged swords of Middle Eastern origin.

clue.text: Second kind of soldier, good and smart

parts.note: a tin soldier is a toy figure

explanation.surface: A second sort of soldier is described as good and well turned out.
explanation.walkthrough: Smart looks like an adjective for a soldier, but it is the verb meaning to hurt.
explanation.definitionFit: To smart is to feel a sharp pain, just as a wound or insect bite does.

clue.text: Irish author or 24, for example

definitions.meaning: first meaning: Oliver, the Irish writer of The Vicar of Wakefield
second meaning: Cellini was a craftsman in precious metal

explanation.walkthrough: Cellini, the answer at 24, was a Renaissance worker in precious metal.
explanation.definitionFit: Oliver Goldsmith was an Irish novelist and playwright, and a craftsman working in precious yellow metal has the same trade name.

clue.text: Mix our two tins to provide nourishment

indicators.note: mixing stirs the letters together into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
the word tin twice over

explanation.surface: Combining the contents of two tins with ours makes a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Nutrition is the food or process that keeps a body nourished.

clue.text: Affect with drug, producing odd reaction laced with sulphur

indicators.note: laced with sulphur means the sulphur is mixed in, set inside the rearranged letters
an odd reaction is a strange one, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A drugged drink produces a strange response because it was spiked with sulphur.
explanation.definitionFit: To narcotise is to put someone under the influence of a stupefying substance.

clue.text: At home abstaining, having drunk cider inside bar

parts.note: in means at home

indicators.note: the jumbled drink goes inside the abstainer's letters

parts.note: TT stands for teetotal

indicators.note: drunk suggests something scrambled, so the letters of cider are mixed up

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A teetotaller at home has nonetheless been drinking cider in a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: Bar looks like a pub, which the cider encourages, but it is the verb meaning to prohibit.
explanation.definitionFit: To interdict is to forbid or prohibit something formally.

clue.text: eg restyle, after conversion, in bluish colour

indicators.note: converted letters are changed into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An example: restyling something, once converted, in a bluish shade.
explanation.definitionFit: This shade is the dull bluish grey of the alloy made from iron and carbon.

clue.text: Encountered 6 as an example of this

definitions.text: Encountered 6 as an example of this

parts.note: met means encountered
the answer at 6 is aluminium, whose chemical symbol is Al

explanation.surface: Someone met an instance of a category.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also defines: aluminium, the answer at 6, is an example of what is being built.
explanation.definitionFit: Aluminium is a lightweight element in the class of malleable, conductive substances.

clue.text: Adjusts minimal amounts of elements, including uranium in small quantities

indicators.note: the atoms include, or hold inside, the rest

parts.note: an atom is the smallest unit of a chemical element

indicators.note: uranium goes in among the small quantities

parts.note: cc, cubic centimetres, are small volumes; CCS is the plural

explanation.surface: A chemist tweaks tiny amounts of elements, with uranium in small measures.
explanation.definitionFit: To accustom someone is to adapt or habituate them to something.

clue.text: Religious leader symbolically lists three elements and start of another

wordplay.words: symbolically lists three elements and start of another
wordplay.note: Ca, Li and F are the symbols for calcium, lithium and fluorine, and together they also start the name of californium

explanation.surface: A cleric spells out three elements by their symbols and begins a fourth.
explanation.walkthrough: Both readings give the same letters: three symbols run together, which are also the opening of californium.
explanation.definitionFit: A calif, or caliph, was the Muslim ruler regarded as successor to Muhammad.

clue.text: Prepare drink for 007, something fermented with hydrogen in it

indicators.note: the hydrogen goes in it, the fermented drink

parts.note: sake is fermented Japanese rice wine

explanation.surface: Making James Bond's drink from fermented liquor laced with hydrogen.
explanation.walkthrough: 007 is James Bond, whose martini is famously shaken, not stirred.
explanation.definitionFit: James Bond orders his martini made by agitating it vigorously, never stirred.

clue.text: Words like iron and lead, perhaps, but not cobalt and tungsten

definitions.text: Words like iron and lead, perhaps
definitions.meaning: iron and lead are metals but can also be action words: to iron, to lead
cobalt and tungsten cannot be used as action words

explanation.walkthrough: The metals mislead: the clue is about parts of speech, and only some metal names double as doing words.
explanation.definitionFit: Iron and lead can name actions in a sentence, whereas cobalt and tungsten are only ever nouns.

clue.text: Part of silver necklace for French author

indicators.note: only part of the phrase silver necklace is taken, a run of letters within it

parts.note: the French writer's name runs across the end of silver and the start of necklace

explanation.surface: A piece of a silver necklace belonging to a French writer.
explanation.definitionFit: Jules Verne was the French novelist behind Around the World in Eighty Days.

clue.text: Famous metalworker and I put in small room with nickel

indicators.note: the letter I is put inside the room and nickel together

parts.note: a cell is a small room, as in a prison or monastery
taken as written

explanation.surface: A famous craftsman and the speaker are locked in a cell with nickel.
explanation.definitionFit: Benvenuto Cellini was a Renaissance Italian goldsmith and sculptor.

clue.text: Prepare to try gas (not oxygen) when containing bad air

indicators.note: the gas, without oxygen, contains the jumbled air
not means the element named is left out of the gas

parts.note: argon is a noble gas

indicators.note: bad suggests the letters of air are spoiled into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Getting ready to test a gas, minus oxygen, that holds polluted air.
explanation.walkthrough: Try is the legal sense: to put on trial.
explanation.definitionFit: To arraign is to call an accused person before a court to answer a charge, the step before a trial.
